_note: AI-drafted Call to Worship — pending Wilson's curation.

registers.label: Spare
lines: They set the child in a basket and trusted him to the river.
If the Lord had not been on our side.
The water rose against us, and we were not swept away.
Our help is in the name of the Lord.
Who do you say that I am? Jesus asks.
You are the Messiah, the Son of the living God.
Come, let us worship on this rock.
We come, and we confess. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Feel the solid rock beneath your feet after the flood, the ground that does not give way when the water rises.
On this rock we stand.
A mother laid her baby in the reeds of the Nile and let the current carry him toward a mercy she could not see.
On this rock we stand.
If the Lord had not been on our side, the psalmist sings, the torrent would have gone clean over us.
On this rock we stand.
And Jesus asks the question straight to your face, who do you say I am — and on your answer the church is built.
On this rock we stand. You are the Messiah, the Son of the living God!

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: A child trusted to the river, and drawn out alive.
On this rock we stand.
The flood rose, and we were not swept away.
On this rock we stand.
Who do you say I am? You are the Messiah.
On this rock we stand.
Come, let us worship and confess his name.
On this rock we stand. Amen.
